```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Check that every section of HEALTH-CHECK.md reaches `gh` carrying its labels.
#
# Runs the real filing script with a stub `gh` first on PATH, so it needs no
# credentials and files nothing. The stub is worth its length because the bug
# this guards against is entirely in how gh reads --label: gh splits the value
# on commas itself and does *not* trim, so a single `--label "bug, dead-code"`
# asks for a label named " dead-code", fails the whole call, and drops the
# issue into the unlabelled fallback. Asserting on the argv alone would pass a
# script that still merged the labels into one argument.
#
#   bash scripts/file-health-check-issues.test.sh
#
# Deliberately not wired into `npm test`: that suite is `tsc` plus `node --test`
# over compiled TypeScript, and this needs bash 4, GNU grep -P and a writable
# TMPDIR, none of which the repo asks of a developer's host today.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
REPORT="$ROOT/HEALTH-CHECK.md"
[ -f "$REPORT" ] || { echo "No $REPORT" >&2; exit 1; }

TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$TMP/bin" "$TMP/calls"

cat >"$TMP/bin/gh" <<'STUB'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stand-in for gh. `issue list` reports nothing exists, so nothing is skipped;
# `issue create` validates its labels the way the real one does — comma-split,
# no trimming, exact match against the labels a repo defines — and records the
# call at "$CALLS/created" as "<title><TAB><labels separated by spaces>".
set -euo pipefail
KNOWN=" bug dead-code documentation security dependencies ui "

case "${1:-} ${2:-}" in
  "issue list") exit 0 ;;
  "issue create") shift 2 ;;
  *) echo "stub gh: unexpected invocation: $*" >&2; exit 64 ;;
esac

title=""
labels=()
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo|--body) shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --label)
      IFS=',' read -r -a parts <<<"$2"
      labels+=("${parts[@]}")
      shift 2 ;;
    *) echo "stub gh: unexpected argument [$1]" >&2; exit 64 ;;
  esac
done

for label in ${labels[@]+"${labels[@]}"}; do
  case "$KNOWN" in
    *" $label "*) ;;
    *) echo "stub gh: could not add label: '$label' not found" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

printf '%s\t%s\n' "$title" "${labels[*]:-}" >>"$CALLS/created"
STUB
chmod +x "$TMP/bin/gh"

: >"$TMP/calls/created"
CALLS="$TMP/calls" PATH="$TMP/bin:$PATH" "$ROOT/scripts/file-health-check-issues.sh" \
  >"$TMP/stdout" 2>"$TMP/stderr" || {
    echo "FAIL: the filing script exited non-zero" >&2
    cat "$TMP/stderr" >&2
    exit 1
  }

# The expectation is re-derived from the report rather than hard-coded, so a
# later health check can replace HEALTH-CHECK.md wholesale without this rotting.
failures=0
while read -r n; do
  title="$(grep -oP "^### $n\. \K.*" "$REPORT")"
  want="$(awk -v n="$n" '
    $0 ~ "^### " n "\\. " { grab = 1; next }
    grab && /^### / { exit }
    grab && /^---$/ { exit }
    grab && /^\*\*Labels:\*\* / { sub(/^\*\*Labels:\*\* /, ""); print; exit }
  ' "$REPORT" | awk -F',' '{
    out = ""
    for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) {
      s = $i
      gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", s)
      if (s != "") out = (out == "" ? s : out " " s)
    }
    print out
  }')"

  # ENVIRON rather than -v: awk expands backslash escapes in a -v value, and
  # these titles are prose lifted straight out of the report.
  count="$(t="$title" awk -F'\t' '$1 == ENVIRON["t"] { n++ } END { print n + 0 }' "$TMP/calls/created")"
  if [ "$count" != "1" ]; then
    echo "FAIL: section $n was filed $count times, expected once" >&2
    failures=$((failures + 1))
    continue
  fi

  got="$(t="$title" awk -F'\t' '$1 == ENVIRON["t"] { print $2 }' "$TMP/calls/created")"
  if [ "$got" != "$want" ]; then
    echo "FAIL: section $n filed with labels [$got], expected [$want]" >&2
    failures=$((failures + 1))
  fi
done < <(grep -oP '^### \K[0-9]+(?=\.)' "$REPORT")

if [ "$failures" != 0 ]; then
  echo "$failures section(s) reached gh with the wrong labels" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "ok: every section of HEALTH-CHECK.md reached gh with its labels intact"
```
